question.worked_solution:
To save time, we will keep the variable on the right-hand side as we solve. First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $1$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}16 & =3y+1 \\ 16-1 & =3y+1-1 \\ 15 & =3y+0 \\ 15 & =3y\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}15 & =3y \\ \frac{15}{3} & =\frac{3y}{3} \\ 5 & =\frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} \\ 5 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5=y,$ we conclude that the solution is $y=5.$
